answer.rationale: p99 latency is climbing 5x on the write path, confined to the primary region, with a release 2h old and writes at peak. I want to pull memory_b1 before committing because it is the strongest inherited evidence for a rollback as a safe, low-customer-impact remediation under similar conditions (release-induced error spike, prior build stable). With one intervention only, a rollback directly addresses the most likely root cause (recent release on the write path) while preserving customer writes — and memory_b1 says it cleared a similar spike without customer impact. I am not committing to failover or capacity yet: failover is regional and memory_b2 supports it, but a release-driven regression can also recover regionally without the cost of a traffic shift during peak settlement. Adding capacity (memory_b3) or enabling a circuit breaker (memory_b4) could help but neither targets the probable regression source and circuit breaking writes would risk losing customer writes, which violates the primary objective. I am also not routing reads because writes are the hot path and memory_b5 is about read-heavy dashboards, not the current symptom. I am keeping downstream value risk flagged because a rollback carries some residual blast radius; I want one verification pass on memory_b1 to confirm the prior outcome held under comparable write-path conditions. If verification weakens the case for rollback, I will reassess, but based on current signals and the inherited record, rollback remains the single highest-leverage safe action.
